item: Same-system comparison of the subtype selectivity of the GABA-A positive modulators under discussion
decisive_datum: whether N-desmethylclobazam is alpha2-preferring in efficacy (rat HEK293, Ralvenius 2016), non-selective (human oocytes, Hammer 2015) or modestly alpha2-preferring in affinity (Jensen 2014) [ADV-004 2026-11-14] data exist; the selectivity is basis-dependent and not shown to reproduce across laboratories; alpha2-preferring is not established (alpha2/alpha1 for N-desmethylclobazam is above 1 in both functional papers: 1.77 printed, 1.33 total or 1.65 increment derived; the alpha2-against-alpha1 contrast in Ralvenius is also beta3 against beta2); at least eight assay conditions differ and none is shown to explain it; source gabaa_subtype_adv004_20261114/README.md
queries_and_sources: source: three open primary papers read by the independent verifier; a 2026 phase IIa paper cites Ralvenius 2016 alone, in its Introduction, for the in vitro alpha2 preference (reference list not checked) [ADV-004 2026-11-14]
trigger_to_reopen: a head-to-head in one system with diazepam as comparator (met by Ralvenius 2016 alone, with qualifications; it does not resolve the dispute) [ADV-004 2026-11-14] re-scoped, not closed: an independent same-laboratory series at matched beta with diazepam, clonazepam, clobazam and N-desmethylclobazam at alpha1/2/3/5, a stated EC10 and EC20 with total and increment bases, n per subtype and a defined Emax reference; or an independent replication of the N-desmethylclobazam alpha2/alpha1 ratio; hits that do not address this do not reopen it
